title: The Triangle and Its Properties — Practice Quiz

questions.prompt: A triangle with all three sides equal is called:
questions.explanation: All three sides equal → equilateral. (All angles are also $60°$.)

questions.prompt: The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is:
questions.explanation: The angle sum property: interior angles of every triangle add up to $180°$.

questions.prompt: A triangle with exactly two equal sides is:
questions.explanation: Two equal sides → isosceles. The angles opposite those sides are also equal.

questions.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the longest side (opposite the right angle) is the:
questions.explanation: The side opposite the $90°$ angle is the hypotenuse, and it is the longest side.

questions.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are $50°$ and $70°$. What is the third angle?
A median of a triangle joins a vertex to the:
questions.explanation: A median runs from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. (An altitude is the perpendicular.)

questions.prompt: The two interior angles opposite an exterior angle are $50°$ and $70°$. What is the exterior angle?
questions.explanation: Exterior angle = sum of the two opposite interior angles: $50° + 70° = 120°$.

questions.prompt: Each angle of an equilateral triangle measures:
questions.explanation: Three equal angles summing to $180°$: each is $\dfrac{180°}{3} = 60°$.

questions.prompt: Can a triangle have sides of length $3$, $4$, and $8$?
options: Yes, any three lengths form a triangle
No, because all sides must be equal
questions.explanation: Triangle inequality: the sum of any two sides must exceed the third. $3 + 4 = 7 < 8$, so no triangle is possible.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has legs $3$ and $4$. What is the hypotenuse?
A right triangle has hypotenuse $13$ and one leg $5$. What is the other leg?
An isosceles triangle has a vertex (apex) angle of $40°$. What is each base angle?
questions.explanation: The two base angles are equal and share the remaining $180° - 40° = 140°$. Each is $\dfrac{140°}{2} = 70°$.
